lessons.t: Unit 5 · A Chat with a Grasshopper (ಮಿಡತೆಯೊಂದಿಗೆ ಒಂದು ಮಾತುಕತೆ)
lessons.words: foe – an enemy (ಶತ್ರು); toxic – poisonous (ವಿಷಕಾರಿ); snap – move quickly with a sharp sound (ತಟ್ಟನೆ ಚಲಿಸು); hind – at the back (ಹಿಂಭಾಗದ); weird – strange (ವಿಚಿತ್ರ); dine – eat (ಊಟ ಮಾಡು); weed – a wild plant (ಕಳೆ); striped – marked with long narrow lines (ಗೆರೆಗಳಿರುವ); mate – a partner for breeding (ಜೊತೆ); insane – mad (ಹುಚ್ಚು ಹಿಡಿದಂತಹ)
lessons.notes: Unit 5 (prose: A Chat with a Grasshopper, p. 1–13; poem: The Fly, p. 14–17). Grammar: Wh-questions – what, where, how many, whose, when, why, who (Let's Speak S1 and S3). Words for male, female and young ones of animals (V5). Vocabulary: opposites, homophones, idioms and word-building are practised through the unit's Let's Practise Words section.
ab: Preparatory Activity – 1 Repeat after the teacher: The Grasshopper and the Elephant (p. 1)
Repeat after the teacher: The Grasshopper and the Elephant (poem)
ಶಿಕ್ಷಕರನ್ನು ಅನುಸರಿಸಿ ಪದ್ಯವನ್ನು ಪುನರಾವರ್ತಿಸಿ (ಕಂಠಪಾಠ ಚಟುವಟಿಕೆ).
Preparatory Activity – 2 Can you draw the picture of a grasshopper? What do you know about grasshoppers? (p. 1)
Can you draw the picture of a grasshopper? What do you know about grasshoppers?

ಸೂಚಿತ ಉತ್ತರ: A grasshopper has an exoskeleton, three pairs of strong legs, two pairs of wings and five eyes.
ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು.
Let's Understand – C1 Read the questions and discuss the answers (p. 6)
What helps a grasshopper fly?
Its two sets of wings help it to fly.
How many wings does a grasshopper have?
A grasshopper has four wings (two sets of wings).
How many eyes does a grasshopper have?
A grasshopper has five eyes.
How long are the world's largest grasshoppers?
The world's largest grasshoppers are about 90 mm long (the female is 60–90 mm).

Grasshopper makes a chirping sound by: a) rubbing two legs together b) rubbing one of its legs along one of its wings c) rubbing its wings together d) rubbing its back leg against one of its antennae.
b) rubbing one of its legs along one of its wings. (ಪಠ್ಯದ ಪ್ರಕಾರ ಹಿಂಗಾಲನ್ನು ಮುಂಗಡ ರೆಕ್ಕೆಗೆ ಉಜ್ಜುವುದು. ಆಯ್ಕೆ d ನಲ್ಲಿ 'antennae' ಎಂಬುದು ತಪ್ಪು ಮುದ್ರಣ – 'wing' ಇರಬೇಕು.)
Say True or False: A grasshopper is blind and deaf.
False. A grasshopper has five eyes and can sense vibrations through its antennae.
Grasshoppers do not have ears, yet they can pick up vibrations. How?
They pick up vibrations from the air and the ground with their antennae.
Let's Practise Words – V1 Circle the words used in the lesson (p. 7)
farmer, toxic, exoskeleton, strong, fruits, vibration, weird, turnbull, housefly, insecticide – Which of these words are used in the lesson?
Used in the lesson: farmer, toxic, exoskeleton, strong, vibration, weird, turnbull. Not used: fruits, housefly, insecticide.
Let's Practise Words – V2 Find words from the lesson with the given meanings (p. 7)
a) grain used to make flour  b) poisonous to eat or drink  c) an enemy  d) outside skin of an animal body  e) two long thin parts on the heads of some insects
a – wheat; b – toxic; c – foe; d – exoskeleton; e – antennae

2. The grasshoppers make sounds of ________ on a summer night.

3. The ________ organ can pick up vibrations from the air and on the ground.
antennae

1. The insects that make the sound of buzz ________ [bees, mosquitoes, spiders, caterpillars]
bees
2. The insects that irritate at night ________
mosquitoes
3. The insects that build their own webs ________
spiders
4. The insects that reform as butterflies ________
caterpillars

Read the lesson once more. Write a short paragraph about grasshoppers in five to six sentences.

b), c), d) Read aloud, correct mistakes, make a neat copy
ತರಗತಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಓದುವುದು, ತಪ್ಪುಗಳನ್ನು ತಿದ್ದುವುದು ಮತ್ತು ನೀಟ್ ಪ್ರತಿ ಮಾಡುವುದು (ಶಿಕ್ಷಕರ ಮೇಲ್ವಿಚಾರಣೆ).
Let's Write – W2 I Filling in a Web Diagram: the white tiger (p. 9)
Fill in the bubbles of the web diagram with the most important facts about the white tiger (colour, size, habits, features, habitat).

Colour: creamy white fur with red stripes. Size: about 3 metres long; weighs about 180–258 kg. Features: blue eyes and a pink nose. Habitat: grassy or swampy areas and forests (mainland of south-east Asia, central and southern India). Habits: good swimmers, poor climbers, solitary animals who mostly hunt at night.
Let's Write – W2 II Sit in pairs and write two sentences on how the tiger can be saved (p. 10)
How can the tiger be saved? (write two sentences)
ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು.

e.g. What does a grasshopper eat? (what/eat) – example given

(where/live)

How many eyes does a grasshopper have?
Let's Speak – S2 Show the picture cards and ask two or three questions (p. 11)
Show picture cards of animals/birds/objects and ask two or three questions to your friends.
ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು.
Let's Speak – S3 Read the statements and frame questions using the clues (p. 11–12)
A: My father is a teacher.  B: ________? (what) – example given
What is your father?
A: I like blue colour.  B: ________? (what)
What colour do you like?
A: This book is (mine).  B: ________? (whose)
Whose book is this?
A: We celebrate Vanamahotsava on June 5th.  B: ________? (when)
When do you celebrate Vanamahotsava?
A: Deon likes cows because they give us milk.  B: ________? (why)

A: Sachin is my favourite batsman.  B: ________? (who)

A: Naija goes to school every day.  B: ________? (where)

Let's Speak – S4 Read the instructions/warnings aloud and write where you see them (p. 12)
Write some more instructions/slogans you know.
ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು.
Where do you see: Beware of dogs?
At the gate or entrance of a house or a compound wall.
Where do you see: Thanks for not smoking?
In public places such as hospitals, offices, buses and waiting rooms.
Where do you see: Leave your footwear outside?
At the entrance of a house or a place of worship.
Where do you see: Switch off your mobile phone?
In hospitals, libraries, cinema halls and classrooms.
Extended Activity – And …what? (p. 13)
Topic: fruits, vegetables and eatables – I went to the shop and bought…
Each learner adds one more item to the sentence (e.g. I went to the shop and bought mangoes, bananas and rice).
Topic: toys and gift items – For my birthday I got…
Each learner adds one more item to the sentence.
Topic: Birds and animals – I saw… in the forest.
Each learner adds one more item to the sentence.
Further Reading – Poem: Hurt No Living Thing (p. 13)
Read the poem, find the meanings of new words with a dictionary and tell the class.
ನಿಘಂಟಿನ ಸಹಾಯದಿಂದ ಹೊಸ ಪದಗಳ ಅರ್ಥ ತಿಳಿದು ತರಗತಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಹೇಳಿ.

lessons.t: Unit 6 · Where There is a Will, There is a Way (ಇಚ್ಛೆ ಇದ್ದರೆ ದಾರಿ ಇದೆ)
lessons.words: thrilled – excited (ಪುಳಕಿತ); event – an important happening (ಘಟನೆ); exciting – causing strong feelings (ರೋಮಾಂಚಕ); participate – take part in (ಭಾಗವಹಿಸು); victim – one who suffers pain or disability as a result of an accident or disease (ಬಲಿಪಶು); massage – pressing or rubbing to remove pain (ಮಸಾಜ್); gazelle – deer-like animal (ಜಿಂಕೆ); recommend – suggest, advise (ಶಿಫಾರಸು ಮಾಡು); sprinter – fast runner (ವೇಗದ ಓಟಗಾರ); spikes – pointed pieces of metal on running shoes (ಮೊನೆಯಾದ ಲೋಹದ ಮುಳ್ಳುಗಳು); decathlon – a competition where athletes take part in ten events (ದಶಕ್ರೀಡೆ); strike – hit (ಹೊಡೆ); might – strength (ಶಕ್ತಿ); gaze – look (ದಿಟ್ಟಿಸು); stumble – trip and lose balance (ಎಡವು); oft – often (ಆಗಾಗ್ಗೆ); downcast – disgraced (ನಿರಾಶೆಗೊಂಡ); succeed – win (ಯಶಸ್ವಿಯಾಗು)
lessons.notes: Unit 6 (prose: Where There is a Will, There is a Way, p. 18–30; poem: The Way to Succeed, p. 35–41). Grammar: Adverbs of manner (V7 – happily, politely, carefully, etc.); conjunctions 'and' and 'but' (W1); homophones (V2: knew/new, would/wood, won/one); the Listening text on p. 79 is the same as the Unit 6 listening passage.
ab: Let's Listen and Respond (p. 18)
1. What is a website?
A website is a place on the Internet where you can find information about something.
2. Who is Dr Vinod Sena?
Dr Vinod Sena is a visually challenged man (a retired English professor from Delhi University) who has developed a website for the blind.
3. How did Dr Vinod Sena connect the visually challenged people to the world of the internet?
He developed a website that can be navigated without a mouse. With text-to-speech software it becomes audio-based, so visually challenged people can use it without sighted help.
4. Do you know any other specially abled persons who have done great things in their lives? Describe the achievements of such persons.
ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು.
Let's Understand – C1 Choose the right answer from the four alternatives (p. 22–23)
1. Wilma Rudolf is famous as: a. the runner on wheels b. a disabled person c. a wrestler d. black gazelle
d. black gazelle (ಪಠ್ಯದಲ್ಲಿ 'c. a wrestler' ಆಯ್ಕೆಯು Q1 ಗೆ ಸೇರಿದ್ದು – ಸರಿಪಡಿಸಲಾಗಿದೆ)
2. Wilma is a ____: a. dancer b. sprinter c. singer d. teacher
b. sprinter
3. Wilma's legs were weak because: a. she was injured while playing b. her legs were affected by polio c. her legs were crushed by a machine d. she met with an accident
b. her legs were affected by polio
4. Rafer found it difficult to run: a. with artificial limbs b. using crutches c. with blades tied below his knees d. wearing spiked shoes
d. wearing spiked shoes
5. Decathlon is ____: a. a competition where athletes take part in ten separate events b. a medal given in Olympics c. a place where paralympics is held d. the name of the coach of Rafer Johnson
a. a competition where athletes take part in ten separate events
Let's Understand – C2 Find the answers from the lesson (p. 23)
1. Where was the 1992 Olympics held?
The 1992 Olympics were held in Barcelona.
2. Who are the two athletes that this lesson talks about?
Wilma Rudolf and Rafer Johnson.
3. To which country did Wilma belong?
Wilma belonged to the U.S.A.
4. What was the doctor's recommendation to improve Wilma's legs?
The doctors recommended regular massage of her limp leg.
5. What happened to Rafer's left leg?
When he was twelve, his left leg was badly crushed in a machine.
6. List out the events in decathlon.
100 m dash, long jump, shot put, high jump, 400 m run, 110 m hurdle, discus throw, pole vault, javelin throw, 1500 m run.
Let's Understand – C3 Discuss in groups and answer (p. 23)
1. Many countries send their teams to the Olympics. Why?
It is an honour for any country to send its athletes, and the Olympics is one of the world's biggest events.
2. Why are the players not happy when they just win?
Players want to set a new record and become the world's best ever, so winning alone does not satisfy them.
3. How did Wilma's family help her?
Each member of her family spent time massaging her leg, and in course of time she was able to walk.
4. How did Rafer suffer as a boy?
When he was twelve, his left leg was badly crushed in a machine; the surgeon feared it might have to be cut off, and he had difficulty wearing spiked shoes later.
5. What do you learn from the lives of these two great athletes?
ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು.
6. Have you met anyone who has made great achievement in his / her life? Tell your friends about him / her.
ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು.
Let's Understand – C4 Arrange the details in sequential order and rewrite as a paragraph (p. 24)

Arrange in sequential order: 1. She was in bed for two years. 2. She became well in course of time. 3. Wilma was weak as a baby. 4. She played for her school in one of the matches. 5. She had regular massage of her limp leg. 6. She had an attack of polio in her fourth year.
Rewrite the details as a paragraph.

Wilma was weak when she was born. At the age of four, she had an attack of polio and was in bed for two years. Her family gave her regular massage to her limp leg, and in course of time she was able to walk. She became well and played basketball for her school.

5. Your friend helped you find your missing book. Thank him/her.

Poem – The Way to Succeed: Preparatory Activity (p. 35)
Arrange pebbles, say who put the highest number, what you would do if you fail, and the efforts needed to succeed.
ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು.
Poem – The Way to Succeed: Let's Understand I. 1–6 (p. 37)
1. 'Drive the nail aright, boys ……' What does the statement mean?
It means doing the work carefully, correctly and in the right way.
2. What will happen if one never tries?
One will never reach the goal or succeed; he will stand at the foot of the hill and never climb it.
3. When should we try and try again?
Whenever we stumble or fail, we should not be downcast and should try again.
4. Why should we try and try again?
Because if we keep trying, we will succeed at last.
5. What should one do to reach the top?
One must first climb the hill, that is, work hard step by step.
6. What suggestions does the poet give to succeed in life?
Do the work with a will, strike while the iron is red, never be downcast when you stumble, and keep trying again and again.
Poem – The Way to Succeed: Let's Understand I. 7 True or False (p. 37)
a) The poet says that we must wait for the opportunity before doing anything.
False. The poet says we should do the work with a will, not wait.
b) According to the poet, failure is a stepping stone to success.
True. The poet says 'Though you stumble oft … you'll succeed at last'.
Poem – The Way to Succeed: Let's Understand I. 8 Colour the success words (p. 37)
Colour the words/phrases related to achieving success: give up, work hard, be lazy, be active, lose hope, aim high, be positive, be confident, never try, take help from others, persevere.
Colour: work hard, be active, aim high, be positive, be confident, take help from others, persevere. Do not colour: give up, be lazy, lose hope, never try.
Poem – The Way to Succeed: Let's Understand I. 9 (p. 38)
What do you want to achieve in life? What efforts will you make to achieve this?
ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು.
Poem – The Way to Succeed: II Match the idioms with their meanings (p. 38)
Drive the nail aright
do the work correctly and in the right way
Strike while the iron is red
use the opportunity in the right way while it lasts
Standing at the foot, gazing at the sky
hoping for the best without putting in efforts
Poem – The Way to Succeed: II Complete the sentences by matching columns A and B (p. 38)
1. Drive the nail aright
c) hit it on the head
2. Strike with all your might
d) while the iron is red
3. When you have work to do
e) do it with a will
4. To reach the top
a) one must first climb the hill
5. Though you stumble oft
b) never feel downcast (f – 'you will succeed at last' is the end of this stanza and is an extra option)
Poem – The Way to Succeed: III Standing at the foot, gazing at the sky (p. 38)
Explain the line 'Standing at the foot, gazing at the sky'.
It means standing at the bottom and only looking up without climbing; one must make efforts to reach the top.
Poem – The Way to Succeed: IV Tick the proverbs related to the theme (p. 39)
Where there is a will there is a way
Ticked. If we have a strong desire and effort, we can find a way to achieve our goal.
There is no shortcut to hard work
Ticked. Success comes only through hard work, not through short cuts.
Awake, arise, stop not until you reach your goal
Ticked. We should work continuously until we reach the goal.
An idle mind is a devil's workshop
Ticked. A lazy person gets into trouble; one should always keep busy with useful work.

will – hill; head – red; aright – might; sky – try; downcast – last
Poem – The Way to Succeed: Let's Appreciate 2–4 (p. 39)
2. Mime a line from the poem. 3. Read the poem backwards. 4. Suggest some more titles to the poem.

lessons.t: Unit 7 · Neerja Bhanot: Brave in Life, Brave in Death (ನೀರ್ಜಾ ಭಾನೋಟ್: ಜೀವನದಲ್ಲಿ ಧೈರ್ಯಶಾಲಿ, ಮರಣದಲ್ಲಿಯೂ ಧೈರ್ಯಶಾಲಿ)
lessons.words: attendant – a person employed to provide a service to the public (ಸಿಬ್ಬಂದಿ); on board – on a plane (ವಿಮಾನದಲ್ಲಿ); hijack – take control of a plane by force (ವಿಮಾನ ಅಪಹರಣ); recipient – a person who is awarded something (ಪುರಸ್ಕೃತ); civilian – a person not in the armed services (ನಾಗರಿಕ); alumna – a former woman student (ಹಳೆಯ ವಿದ್ಯಾರ್ಥಿನಿ); purser – an officer on a plane who takes care of passengers (ಗಗನಸಖಿ ಮುಖ್ಯಸ್ಥೆ); en route – on the way (ದಾರಿಯಲ್ಲಿ); cockpit – compartment for the pilot (ಚಾಲಕ ಕೋಣೆ); crew – all the people working on a plane (ವಿಮಾನ ಸಿಬ್ಬಂದಿ); tarmac – runway (ವಿಮಾನ ನಿಲ್ದಾಣದ ರನ್‌ವೇ); flee – run away (ಓಡಿಹೋಗು); take charge – assume control (ಹೊಣೆ ವಹಿಸಿಕೊಳ್ಳು); set off – move to act; put in motion (ಸ್ಫೋಟಿಸು/ಆರಂಭಿಸು); explosive – a substance used in bombs (ಸ್ಫೋಟಕ); shield – protect from danger (ರಕ್ಷಿಸು); hail of bullets – a collection of bullets (ಗುಂಡಿನ ಮಳೆ); distress – anxiety, sorrow, pain (ಸಂಕಟ); lasting – permanent (ಶಾಶ್ವತ); tribute – an act that shows respect (ಗೌರವ ಸಲ್ಲಿಕೆ); citation – official document in praise of a brave act (ಪ್ರಶಸ್ತಿ ಪತ್ರ); centenary – 100th anniversary (ಶತಮಾನೋತ್ಸವ); plaque – a piece of metal given in memory of a person (ಫಲಕ); faint – become unconscious (ಪ್ರಜ್ಞೆತಪ್ಪು); swoon – faint (ಮೂರ್ಛೆ ಹೋಗು); excavate – dig up (ಅಗೆದು ತೆಗೆ); weave – make cloth on a machine (ನೇಯ್ಗೆ ಮಾಡು); plough – a tool used by farmers to turn over soil (ಉಳು); sigh – make a sound when breathing out, often when sad (ನಿಟ್ಟುಸಿರು ಬಿಡು); debt – money owed to someone (ಸಾಲ); misery – sadness and suffering (ಸಂಕಟ); interest – extra money paid when borrowing (ಬಡ್ಡಿ); pay through the nose – pay much more than the real worth (ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಹಣ ತೆರು); suppress – hold back (ಅದುಮಿಡು); ash – grey powder left after burning (ಬೂದಿ); fiery – angry, excited (ಉದ್ರೇಕಕಾರಿ); eat your fill – eat as much as you want (ಹೊಟ್ಟೆ ತುಂಬ ತಿನ್ನು); devote – use time or energy for a purpose (ಅರ್ಪಿಸು)
lessons.notes: Unit 7 (prose: Neerja Bhanot: Brave in Life, Brave in Death, p. 42–48; poem: My People, p. 49–55). Grammar: past tense forms of verbs (G1, G2); helping verbs and articles in sentences (G3). Listening: a news report (p. 84 listening text) on the honour given to Neerja Bhanot. Vocabulary: words related to aircraft and flight (C5); professions (poem preparatory activity).
ab: Preparatory Activity – 1 Look at the picture and describe the woman (p. 42)
Can you describe the woman? Who is she? Where is she from? How does she look? What is her profession?
ಆಕೆ ನೀರ್ಜಾ ಭಾನೋಟ್ – ಪ್ಯಾನ್ ಆಮ್ ವಿಮಾನ ಸಂಸ್ಥೆಯ ಗಗನಸಖಿ (ಏರ್ ಹೋಸ್ಟೆಸ್). ಚಿತ್ರ ನೋಡಿ ವಿವರಿಸಿ. ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು.
Let's Listen (1) – News report: listen and answer (p. 42)
1. Who is the air hostess mentioned in the report?
Neerja Bhanot, a Pan Am air hostess.
2. Who honoured her?
The Civil Aviation Ministry honoured her. Union Minister Vayalar Ravi presented a plaque, shawl and citation to her brother Aneesh Bhanot.
3. Why was she honoured?
She lost her life while saving the passengers of a Pan Am flight that was hijacked by armed terrorists.
4. Who hijacked the plane?
Armed terrorists hijacked the Pan Am flight at Karachi airport.
Preparatory Activity – 3 Narrate one incident of bravery (p. 43)
You have read a lesson in class V about bravery awards. Can you narrate one incident of bravery from the lesson?
ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು.
Let's Understand – Reading questions (p. 43–44)
1. Who were Neerja's parents?
Rama Bhanot and Harish Bhanot. (Her father was a Mumbai-based journalist.)
2. When did she join Pan Am Airlines?
She joined Pan Am Airlines in 1986.
3. Who escaped from the aircraft? Why?
The three-member cockpit crew (pilot, co-pilot and flight engineer) fled from the aircraft, because the plane was on the tarmac when the hijack began and they were able to run away.
4. How did Neerja die?
She died while shielding three children from a hail of bullets, after she had helped many passengers escape.
Let's Understand – C1 Discuss in small groups and answer in a sentence each (p. 45–46)
1. Where did Neerja study?
She studied at Sacred Heart Senior Secondary School (Chandigarh), Bombay Scottish School and St. Xavier's College (Mumbai).
2. Why was the flight described as 'ill-fated'?
Because the flight was hijacked by heavily armed terrorists.
3. Name the highest civilian award for bravery given by the Indian government.
The Ashoka Chakra.
4. Name the flight that was hijacked. When and where did this happen?
Pan Am Flight 73 was hijacked at Karachi airport, after it landed there at 5 a.m. from Mumbai.
5. Who did the terrorists shoot first?
They shot dead a passenger who identified himself as an American.
6. What did the pilot, co-pilot and the flight engineer do when they heard about the hijack? Do you think they were right in doing so?
They fled from the aircraft. ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು. (ಅಭಿಪ್ರಾಯ ಆಧಾರಿತ ಉತ್ತರ)
7. Did Neerja hide the passports of the Americans? Why/Why not?
Yes. She hid the passports of 40 Americans so that the hijackers could not identify and harm the Americans.
8. Why is Neerja called 'the heroine of the hijack'?
She alerted the crew, comforted passengers, hid the passports of the Americans, helped many passengers to escape through the emergency door, and died while shielding three children.
9. What is your ambition in life? Do you want to become an air hostess or a pilot or a flight engineer?
ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು.
Let's Understand – C2 Arrange the sentences to make a meaningful paragraph (p. 46)

1. After 17 hours, the hijackers opened fire and set off explosives. 2. Acting quickly, Neerja opened the emergency door and helped a number of passengers escape. 3. Neerja was the Senior Flight Purser on a Pan Am flight which was hijacked at Karachi airport. 4. She hid the passports of the Americans as the hijackers wanted to execute Americans. 5. Neerja laid down her life, while saving hundreds of others. 6. Neerja comforted the passengers, especially the elderly and small children.
Let's Understand – C3 Tick the true statements about Neerja (p. 46)
1. Neerja was the senior most cabin crew on the aircraft.
True (ticked).
2. Neerja escaped from the flight when the terrorists opened fire.
False. She did not escape; she died while saving others.
3. She showed the passports of all the passengers to the hijackers.
False. She collected and hid the passports of the Americans.
4. She received the Ashoka Chakra award for her act of bravery from the Civil Aviation Minister.
False. The lesson does not say this. The Civil Aviation Minister presented a plaque to her brother at a separate centenary function (news report).
Let's Understand – C4 Write a short paragraph about Neerja in your own words (p. 47)
Write a short paragraph, in your own words, about Neerja.
ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು.
Let's Understand – C5 Circle the words related to airport / flight (p. 47)
crew, driver, runway, kidnap, check-in, pilot, air hostess, cabin, cockpit, overtake, hijack, traffic police depot, emergency door
crew, runway, check-in, pilot, air hostess, cabin, cockpit, hijack, emergency door (driver, kidnap, overtake and traffic police depot are not related)
Let's Practise Language – G1 Find the other forms of the words and write them in the box (p. 47)
Present: die / go / take / hijack / shoot / join / is / land – write the past forms.
died; went; took; hijacked; shot; joined; was; landed
Let's Practise Language – G2 Think of more words and write their past tense forms (p. 47)
Present → Past (add more words)
Sample: play – played; eat – ate; write – wrote; run – ran; see – saw. ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು.
Let's Practise Language – G3 Add the missing words to complete the sentences (p. 48)
Neerja Bhanot ____ a brave woman. (example)
was
1. Neerja Bhanot ____ born in Chandigarh.
was
2. Rama Bhanot and Harish Bhanot ____ her parents.
are
3. She ____ the senior most cabin crew member.
was
4. Neerja ____ the passports of the American passengers.
hid
5. She ____ not escape.
did
6. She ____ youngest recipient of the Ashoka Chakra.
was
Extended Activity – Make sentences using the words from the box (p. 48)
Make sentences using the words from the box. Example: I have visited Hyderabad.
Sample sentences from the box: I have visited Hyderabad. / She can cook roti. / We should respect our parents. / My sister likes to eat roti. / She doesn't speak Hindi. / I have a bicycle.
Poem – My People: Preparatory Activity 1 a) Write the names of the professions (p. 49)
A person who mends shoes.
cobbler
A person who stitches clothes.
tailor
A person who makes ornaments.
goldsmith (jeweller)
A person who represents people in court.
lawyer
A person who works in the field.
farmer
A person who sells fruits and vegetables.
fruit and vegetable vendor
Poem – My People: Preparatory Activity 1 b) and 2 (p. 49)
b) Do you know any other professions? Discuss the nature of work.
ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು.
2. Do you agree with 'The rich are getting richer and the poor are getting poorer'? Discuss in groups.
ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು.
Poem – My People: Let's Understand C1 Answer in a word, phrase or sentence (p. 52)
1. Who are referred to as 'they' in the poem?
The poor, working people (labourers, farmers, weavers and others) whom the poet calls 'my people'.
2. 'They weave cloth, but they go naked.' What does this line mean?
The poor weavers make cloth for others, but they themselves do not have enough clothes to wear.
3. Why do these people sigh?
They live in misery and poverty, come home empty-handed and are in heavy debts.
4. Who does the poet refer to as God-loving men? What do they do?
The privileged, rich people who 'eat their fill'; they make the poor prepare footwear and other goods for them.
5. Is the poet sympathetic to them? How do you know?
Yes. He calls them 'my people' again and again and describes their sufferings with pity.
Poem – My People: Let's Understand C2 Discuss in small groups (p. 53)
1. Who is the speaker in this poem? Who is he talking about?
The poet (Dr Siddalingaiah) speaks, and he talks about the poor working people, 'my people'.
2. What activities are done by these people, as mentioned in the poem?
They carry stones, excavate gold, weave cloth, plough the field, sow seeds, cut crops, build shops and bungalows, prepare footwear and work for others.
3. Why does the poet have sympathy towards these people?
Because they suffer hunger, misery, debts and exploitation, and their hard work does not bring them a good life.
4. Isn't it a pity that some people build the shops but get into heavy debts? How does this happen?
They borrow money and pay very high interest; they cannot repay the debt and remain poor.
5. What should be done to solve the miseries of these people?
ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು.

Have a debate on the given topic.
ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು.

2. Play the role of the poet and interview the poet.
ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು.
Read the poem in original in Kannada by Dr Siddalingaiah.
ಕನ್ನಡ ಮೂಲ ಪದ್ಯವನ್ನು ಓದಿ ಚರ್ಚಿಸಿ (ಚಟುವಟಿಕೆ).

lessons.t: Unit 8 · 'What I Want for You and Every Child' – A Letter from Obama to His Daughters (ಒಬಾಮ ಅವರು ತಮ್ಮ ಪುತ್ರಿಯರಿಗೆ ಬರೆದ ಪತ್ರ)
lessons.words: campaign trail – a series of events a politician does to win an election (ಚುನಾವಣಾ ಪ್ರಚಾರ); parade – a public procession celebrating an event (ಮೆರವಣಿಗೆ); make up for something – take the place of something lost (ಭರ್ತಿ ಮಾಡು); potential – ability that can be developed (ಸಾಮರ್ಥ್ಯ); instill – introduce gradually (ತುಂಬು/ಮೂಡಿಸು); compassionate – showing sympathy and concern for others (ಕರುಣಾಮಯಿ); thrive – grow well (ಅರಳು/ಅಭಿವೃದ್ಧಿ ಹೊಂದು); achievement – something done successfully (ಸಾಧನೆ); dignity – self-respect (ಘನತೆ); sonnet – a poem having 14 lines with a fixed rhyme scheme (ಸಾನೆಟ್); incomparable – extremely good (ಅಪ್ರತಿಮ); contemplate – think about (ಚಿಂತಿಸು); raise – bring up, look after (ಬೆಳೆಸು); hard – difficult (ಕಷ್ಟದ)
lessons.notes: Unit 8 (prose: 'What I Want for You and Every Child' – A Letter from Obama to His Daughters, p. 56–66; poem: A Sonnet for my Incomparable Mother, p. 67–70). Writing: letter format (sender's address, date, salutation, body, closing); jumbled letter and gap-filling letter (W1, W2); planning a personal letter (W3). Grammar: contracted forms and their full forms (S1); polite expressions in dialogues (S2).
ab: Preparatory Activity – Fill in the blanks while listening to the poem 'Dear Grown-ups' (p. 56)
Grown-ups
Please leave all the ______ there
flowers
And don't ______ down the trees.
cut
We need the trees to make ______ ______
fresh air
Please don't always use your ______ / To take you everywhere.
car
And ______ the atmosphere. (fumes go very far)
heat
And all the ______ will die.
plants
So please get out and ______ a lot
walk
Then we will run and jump and play / And grow up ______ and ______
strong; tall
Then we'll be ______ everyday
happy
With love from the ______.
children
Let's Understand – C1 Discuss in groups and answer (p. 60)
1. How old were Obama's daughters when he wrote this letter to them?
Malia was 10 and Sasha was 7.
2. What fun did Obama's daughters have when he was on the campaign trail?
They went to picnics, parades and state fairs, and ate junk food.
3. What is the 'journey' that Obama is referring to?
The journey is his decision to contest for the President's post and take his family along on this new life.
4. What fun did his daughters have when he was campaigning for the elections?
They enjoyed picnics, parades, state fairs and junk food during the campaign.
5. What, for Obama, is the greatest joy in life?
The greatest joy in his life is the joy he sees in his daughters' happiness.
6. What did he think as a young man?
He thought life was all about himself: making his way in the world, becoming successful and getting the things he wanted.
7. What did he realize after the birth of his daughters?
He realized that his life would not count for much unless he ensured that his daughters had every opportunity for happiness and fulfilment.
8. Why did he contest for the President's post?
Because of what he wants for his daughters and for every child in the nation.
9. What does he expect his daughters to do?
He expects them to grow into compassionate, committed women who will help build a world with no limits.
10. What is the 'great adventure' referred to in the letter?
The great adventure is the new life of the family in the White House, after he became the President.
Let's Understand – C2 Discuss in small groups and present to the class (p. 60)
1. How did Obama's daughters change his view of the world?
They made him realise that life is not only about himself; he found his greatest joy in their joy.
2. What does Obama want for all the children?
Good schools that challenge them, a chance to go to college, good jobs, a cleaner planet and freedom from the divides of race, region, gender and religion.
3. Why did Obama write this letter to his daughters?
To tell his daughters why he decided to contest for President and what he wants for them and for every child.
4. How do you feel when you read this letter?
ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು.
5. Which line appeals to you the most in this letter?
ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು.

Parts: a) Your loving niece  b) 20 January 2017  c) (body: I write this letter to thank you…)  d) My dear uncle  e) Salma  f) Mysuru
f – b – d – c – a – e (Mysuru, 20 January 2017, My dear uncle, body of the letter, Your loving niece, Salma)

You know, I am selected as the ______ of the class.

grandma

Don't worry
A very ______ ______ once again, grandpa!
happy birthday
______ Yours, Pappu
Take care
Let's Write – W3 Write a letter to your friend or cousin about a story, drama, TV programme or film you liked (p. 62–63)
Write a letter to your friend or cousin about a story/drama/TV programme/film that you liked. Plan the letter using the given points.
ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು.

you've – ?

has not

Find a few more contracted forms from the letter: I've (missed/taken)

Let's Speak – S2 Read the dialogue aloud and have similar conversations (p. 64)
a. Practice reading the dialogue aloud (Sneha and Anil).
Read aloud with correct pronunciation and intonation (ಶಿಕ್ಷಕರ ಮೇಲ್ವಿಚಾರಣೆ).
b. Have similar conversations with your friends.
ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು.
Explain: 'I'd better not.'
I had better not (I'd = I had). It is a polite way of refusing.

Poem – A Sonnet: Let's Understand C1 Answer in a word, a phrase or a sentence (p. 69)
1. Who is the poet talking to?
The poet is talking to her mother ('Mom').
2. What makes the poet think of her childhood?
Being a mother herself now, she remembers how her mother raised her with hard work and love.
3. Which word in the poem means: a) great love and loyalty? b) protection?
a) devotion; b) security
4. Fill in the blank: The mother ____ many things to look after her child.
gave
5. What is the most difficult thing that the poet talks about?
Letting her child separate and set her free (letting her grow independent).
6. State true or false: 1. The poet is still a child.
False. The poet is now a mother herself.
6. State true or false: 2. The poet shows her affection and admiration for her mother.
True.
Poem – A Sonnet: Let's Understand C2 Discuss in small groups (p. 69–70)
1. What qualities has the poet imbibed from her mother?
Hard work, sacrifice, devotion, love, strength, patience and selflessness.
2. 'You let me separate and set me free.' What is the meaning of this line?
The mother allowed her child to grow up, become independent and go out into the world.
3. What does the poet say in the last two lines?
She says she tries her best to be a mother like the mother she had.
4. Who do you admire the most in your life? Why?

lessons.notes: Supplementary Reading lesson 2 (p. 71–77 and Let's Understand, p. 76). Words: abbreviations and their full forms (p. 77). Speaking: short discussion questions (p. 77). Note: the textbook gives no picture for the map task; the location answers come from the text.
ab: Preparatory Activity – 1 Locate the places on the Karnataka map (p. 71)
Locate Bengaluru, Mysuru, Ramanagara and Channapatna on the Karnataka map.
Bengaluru and Mysuru are big cities. Channapatna is a small town between Bengaluru and Mysuru. Ramanagara is near Bengaluru (Janapada Loka is near Ramanagara).
Preparatory Activity – 2 Have you visited Channapatna? What is it famous for? (p. 71)
Have you ever visited Channapatna? What is Channapatna famous for?
Channapatna is famous for its beautiful and colourful toys. ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು.
Let's Understand – Answer briefly (p. 76)
1. Which organization is helping the toy makers?
KSHDC (Karnataka State Handicrafts Development Corporation) is giving training to the toy makers.
2. How were the toys made in olden days?
People used to chip away on a piece of wood by hand.
3. How are the toys made in 'Maya Organic' now?
Workers chip away on power lathes and make the toys.
4. What is the opinion of Mr. Girish about toy making?
He is proud of the family's toy-making tradition; he says the toys are world famous and protected as a Geographical Indication (GI).
5. How did the toy industry originate in Channapatna?
Tippu Sultan brought Persian toy makers to his kingdom. They trained local artisans and left this art in the state.
6. What is special about Channapatna toys?
Vegetable colours are used in them, and they are sent to foreign countries.
7. What type of wood is used to make Channapatna toys?
Aale Mara (ivory wood), the Wrightia tinctoria tree.
8. What is special about the Lacquerware craft complex?
The Government of Karnataka constructed it on Tatte Kere Road as a lacquerware craft complex where craft items are made.
9. What do the toy makers make besides toys?
Cricket bats, wickets, photo frames, trophy bases and spectacle holders.
10. How is the Karnataka government helping the artisans?
Through training by KSHDC, a lacquerware craft complex, and financial assistance with the help of the Dutch Government and the 'VISHWA' scheme.

ab: Extended Activity – Pronunciation (p. 78)
1. a. I live in this place. / b. I will leave this place.
live /lɪv/ (ಜೀವಿಸು) – leave /liːv/ (ಬಿಡು): ಎರಡು ಪದಗಳ ಉಚ್ಚಾರಣೆ ಬೇರೆ.
2. a. I want to go. / b. I won't go.
want /wɒnt/ – won't /wəʊnt/: 'won't' ಎಂಬುದು 'will not' ನ ಸಂಕ್ಷಿಪ್ತ ರೂಪ.
3. a. Elephants have short tails. / b. Children are fond of folk tales.
tails (ಬಾಲ) – tales (ಕಥೆಗಳು): ಉಚ್ಚಾರಣೆ ಒಂದೇ ರೀತಿ, ಅರ್ಥ ಬೇರೆ.
4. a. Are you sailing in a boat? / b. Would you like to sell the boat?
sailing (ನೌಕಾಯಾನ) – sell (ಮಾರು): ಸ್ವರದ ಉಚ್ಚಾರಣೆ ಬೇರೆ.
5. a. I always wait for my friend. / b. My weight is 32 kgs.
wait (ಕಾಯು) – weight (ತೂಕ): ಉಚ್ಚಾರಣೆ ಒಂದೇ ರೀತಿ, ಅರ್ಥ ಬೇರೆ.
